traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 2, 2nd ed., 1959), family 358 Commelinaceae: perennial herbs; leaves with a closed papery sheath at the base; flowers usually regular, rarely irregular (Commelina), bisexual, in clusters in the axils or mostly in cymes or panicles at the tips, often blue or white; perianth plainly of two whorls of 3, the outer sepal-like, the inner petal-like; stamens 6 or fewer; ovary always superior, of 3 (rarely 2) cells; fruit a thin capsule, rarely fleshy.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Commelinaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Cartonemataceae: how long the leaves last (character 37), coded evergreen. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Commelinaceae with Cartonemataceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other. Its flowers are not mostly zygomorphic, so a plant of it states its own symmetry; one that is zygomorphic draws this kind, and one stating none is drawn regular.
